# 金胎兩界師資相承

**ID:** X1073
**Volume:** X59
**Category:** 密教部類
**Original Category:** 諸宗著述部／真言宗
**Byline:** 唐 海雲集
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 618–907
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X1073

## Contributors
- 海雲 (A000938)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle (1卷) **Esoteric lineage-record** compiled by **Hǎiyún** [海雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B5%B7%E9%9B%B2), a late-Tang Esoteric Buddhist monk, recording in parallel the master-and-disciple lineages of the two great Tang Esoteric transmission-cycles: the **Vajradhātu** (*Jīngāngjiè* 金剛界) and the **Garbhadhātu** (*Tāizàngjiè* 胎藏界). Preserved as **X59 no. 1073** in the *Xùzàngjīng*. The work is alternately preserved under the longer title *Liǎngbù dàfǎ xiāngchéng shīzī fùfǎ jì* 兩部大法相承師資付法記 ([KR6r0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0115)).

**Abstract**

The work is presented as two parallel lineage-trees:

- **Vajradhātu (Jīngāngjiè 金剛界):** Mahāvairocana 遮那 → Vajrasattva 金薩 → Nāgārjuna 龍猛 → Nāgabodhi 龍智 → Vajrabodhi 金剛智 [跋折羅菩提](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B7%8B%E6%8A%98%E7%BE%85%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90) → Amoghavajra 不空 [不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA) → and on to the Tang ninth-century Esoteric ācāryas.
- **Garbhadhātu (Tāizàngjiè 胎藏界):** the parallel transmission descending through Mahāvairocana → Avalokiteśvara → Nāgārjuna → ... → Śubhakarasiṃha 善無畏 → Yīxíng 一行 [一行](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%80%E8%A1%8C) → and on to the Tang ninth-century Esoteric ācāryas.

The *Xiāngchéng* is one of the principal late-Tang sources for the institutional self-understanding of the Esoteric school as a *liǎngbù* 兩部 (dual-realm) tradition with two distinct but parallel master-disciple genealogies converging in the Tang Chángān monastic establishment. Composition: late ninth century, before the An-Shǐ rebellion's broader disruptions.

The work is paralleled by *Tāijīn liǎngjiè xuèmài* 胎金兩界血脈 ([KR6j0749](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0749)) by [造玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%A0%E7%8E%84), dated 865 CE — together they constitute the principal surviving Tang Esoteric *xiāngchéng / xuèmài* genealogical literature.
